source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Adivamshavatarana sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.61.1–102 and 1.62.1–3, 1.63.1 (GRETIL e-text of the constituted text, lab/ce; star passages and appendix lines are apparatus and were not used; Ganguli (vulgate) only as a reading aid): the king asks to hear, in order, the births among men of gods, danavas, yakshas and rakshasas (1.61.1–2: `asked`); the list of danavas born as kings: Viprachitti as Jarasandha (1.61.4), Hiranyakashipu as Shishupala (1.61.5), and on to 1.61.61 ("dark powers came down too"; the two names on plaques); Drona from a portion of Brihaspati (1.61.63; plaque only); the eight Vasus born to Ganga as Shantanu's sons, by Vasishtha's curse and Indra's order, Bhishma the last of them (1.61.68–69; plaque only); Duryodhana born from a portion of Kali, hated of all the world, by whom the great feud was kindled (1.61.80–81: `kali`, the turn; the name Kali is on the plaque, the voice says "the spirit of strife"); his brothers, a hundred with Duhshasana first, were Paulastyas, that is rakshasas (1.61.82–83; not voiced); Yudhishthira a portion of Dharma, Bhimasena of the Wind, Arjuna of the king of the gods (1.61.84), Nakula and Sahadeva of the two Ashvins (1.61.85: `five`: the hook counts the twin Ashvins as two, so five gods); Karna, born wearing armour, a portion of the Sun (1.61.89: `karna`); of Narayana, the eternal god of gods, a portion was Vasudeva among men (1.61.90: `krishna`; the name Narayana is on the plaque; the text says Vasudeva; Krishna is the same man's familiar name); Baladeva a portion of the serpent Shesha (1.61.91; not used); a portion of Shri born in Drupada's family from the middle of an altar (1.61.95: `draupadi`; the text does not name her in this verse; verse 97 calls her the one who stirs the hearts of five lords of men); whoever hears this descent of the portions, knowing origin and end, does not sink in hardships (1.61.101–102: `payoff`); Janamejaya then asks for the Kuru line from its beginning (1.62.1–2) and the answer opens on a king going to a forest with his army (1.62.3, 1.63.1: the cliffhanger). CE AGAINST THE CATALOG PLAN: the plan had "Vidura of Dharma"; in this chapter the CE reads atres tu … viduram (1.61.79: a son of Atri); Vidura is left out. ORDER: the CE's list runs danavas first, then gods; we open on the five brothers (1.61.84–85) and put Duryodhana at the turn; the source line names the chapter. Chapters 1.59–60 (the genealogies of gods and creatures) are passed over, and the source line says so. KALI here is the male spirit of the age of strife (kali), not the goddess Kali (Kālī): the plaque says so.
structure: As from episode 41 (script/ARC-41-50.md, script/ARC-51-60.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before; no episode of this batch opens on fire) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: Which five gods were the five brothers?
loop.prevQuestion: Which god was born as which hero?
loop.openQuestion: With whom does the king's own family story begin?

strings.recapLine: The gods were told: be born on earth, each in part.
strings.sourceLine: Adi Parva 1.61 · the text lists the demons first · chapters 59–60 passed over · BORI Critical Edition
strings.arcPlaylist: The whole arc is in the Vyasa Begins playlist

lines.note: COLD OPEN (a count; no fire): five warriors stand in a row on a ridge at gold dawn, dark and near; behind each, vast in the sky, a pale standing god. A pull back shows all ten. The card low.

lines.text: The king asked: which god was born as whom?
lines.say: The king asked: [p:200] which god was born as whom?
lines.note: FRAME with the unvoiced recap band (top) · THE CLOSE-UP: the teal hall: Janamejaya's face fills the frame (plaque: Janamejaya · the king who asked): eager, leaning in; as the answer begins the eagerness turns to awe (the brows lift, the lips part): these are his own forefathers.

lines.text: The five Pandava brothers each carried part of a god.
lines.note: STORY: close on the five brothers in a row, a slow track along their faces; their gods stand dim and vast behind (tag: the five Pandavas · sons of Pandu). Split from the next line on 14 Nov (one idea, one caption; the list of gods gets its own picture).

lines.text: The god of justice, the wind, the gods' king, and the twin horsemen.
lines.note: STORY: the same ridge under a pale sky: a track along the row, the gods vast behind the brothers; each god brightens as he is named and his son's plaque arrives beside him (Yudhishthira · Bhima · Arjuna · Nakula and Sahadeva). CE 1.61.84–85 (as the line it was split from).

lines.text: Karna, born in armour, was part of the sun.
lines.say: Karna, [p:100] born in armour, [p:120] was part of the sun.
lines.note: STORY 2 (wedding-turmeric): a tilt up: a lone warrior in a gold breastplate and earrings, his back to a huge low sun in which the Sun god stands in his chariot (plaque: Karna · the warrior born in armour). In the hold, two small plaques, right: Bhishma · last of the eight Vasus; Drona · a part of Brihaspati.

lines.text: And the god above all gods? Part of him came to earth as Krishna.
lines.note: STORY 3 · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (crystal-sky): a crane down from the great dark four-armed god in a bright heaven to a dark young man below in yellow cloth with a peacock feather, standing as the god stands (plaques: Narayana · the eternal god of gods; Krishna · Vasudeva, of the Yadus).

lines.text: But dark powers had been born first. Duryodhana, who lit the feud, was born from the spirit of strife.
lines.say: But dark powers had been born first. [p:300] Duryodhana, [p:80] who lit the feud, [p:120] was born from the spirit of strife.
lines.note: STORY 4 · THE TURN (≈ 50 %) after a real silence · NEW LIGHT (venom-violet): a crowned prince with a mace, seen from below; behind him, where the others had gods, a tall dark shape with a green eye (plaques: Duryodhana · eldest of the hundred Kauravas; KALI · the spirit of strife · not the goddess Kālī). In the hold, two small plaques: Jarasandha · the danava Viprachitti; Shishupala · the daitya Hiranyakashipu. The word of the turn: STRIFE.
lines.gapNote: the comma pause after "feud," measures 0.36 s in the chosen take (limit 0.35): a breath before the main clause, kept

lines.text: A portion of the goddess of fortune rose from an altar: Draupadi.
lines.note: STORY 5 (brahma-rose): a tilt up an altar's low flame to a dark woman in a gold sari rising from its middle, a pale goddess on a lotus vast behind her (plaques: Draupadi · wife of the five brothers; Shri · the goddess of fortune).

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "The wise who hear this do not lose heart in hard times."
lines.say: The wise who hear this [p:150] do not lose heart [p:80] in hard times.
lines.note: THE LIT PAYOFF (a second real silence before it; ≥ 4 s with its hold; seat-ivory): the whole cast at once, lit: the five, Karna, Krishna, Draupadi and the dark prince in one long row under their gods, Vaishampayana small in front with a raised hand (plaque: Vaishampayana · the teller, Vyasa's student); a slow orbit; the hold stays on them (CE 1.61.101–102).

lines.text: The end of an arc · Vyasa Begins
lines.note: The ARC-END CARD (silent): over the lit row, a lacquer cartouche with a flame border: THE END OF AN ARC · VYASA BEGINS · Episodes 47–52 · the playlist line.

lines.text: And now the king wished to hear his own family's story.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger, reworded to the text: 1.62.2, 1.63.1): the king's raised hand in the hall, then a green forest: a crowned rider with a bow at full gallop, deer leaping ahead, the tips of many spears behind him. The source line (top).
